pages.text: While Mama was at the market, Dzigbodi kicked her small ball inside the house, even though Mama had said, “Play ball outside only.” Suddenly, the ball struck the low table, and Mama’s blue cup tumbled down and broke.
sentences: While Mama was at the market, Dzigbodi kicked her small ball inside the house, even though Mama had said, “Play ball outside only.” Suddenly, the ball struck the low table, and Mama’s blue cup tumbled down and broke.
pages.alt: Inside a tidy Ghanaian living room, startled Dzigbodi stands beside her small rubber ball while broken pieces of a blue ceramic cup lie on the floor by a wooden table.

pages.text: Dzigbodi’s heart beat fast. Remembering safety rules, she did not touch the sharp pieces. Instead, she quietly pulled the room door shut. “Maybe Mama will not notice right away,” she thought, yet her tummy began to ache with worry.
sentences: Dzigbodi’s heart beat fast.
Remembering safety rules, she did not touch the sharp pieces.
Instead, she quietly pulled the room door shut.
“Maybe Mama will not notice right away,” she thought, yet her tummy began to ache with worry.
pages.alt: Outside the living room doorway, worried Dzigbodi pulls the wooden door shut with one hand while pressing her other hand against her tummy.

pages.text: All afternoon, Dzigbodi felt heavy and sad. When Mama returned from the market, she noticed at once. “Why are you so quiet today, Dzigbodi?” she asked gently. Dzigbodi nearly stayed silent—then she realised how awful hiding felt.
sentences: All afternoon, Dzigbodi felt heavy and sad.
When Mama returned from the market, she noticed at once.
“Why are you so quiet today, Dzigbodi?” she asked gently.
Dzigbodi nearly stayed silent—then she realised how awful hiding felt.
pages.alt: On the shaded veranda, downcast Dzigbodi twists the hem of her coral dress while Mama sets down her woven market basket and looks at her kindly.

pages.text: “Mama,” she said in a small, trembling voice, “I broke your blue cup because I kicked my ball inside the house. I am truly sorry.” Tears welled in her eyes as she waited, afraid Mama might shout.
sentences: “Mama,” she said in a small, trembling voice, “I broke your blue cup because I kicked my ball inside the house.
I am truly sorry.” Tears welled in her eyes as she waited, afraid Mama might shout.
pages.alt: Dzigbodi standing with bowed head and clasped hands as she confesses honestly to Mama, who sits listening calmly on a carved stool.

pages.text: Mama did not shout. She opened her arms and hugged Dzigbodi warmly. “Thank you for telling me the truth,” she said. “A cup can be bought again, whereas trust cannot. Stay back from the sharp pieces while I pick them up, and please fetch the broom.”
sentences: Mama did not shout.
She opened her arms and hugged Dzigbodi warmly.
“Thank you for telling me the truth,” she said.
“A cup can be bought again, whereas trust cannot.
Stay back from the sharp pieces while I pick them up, and please fetch the broom.”
pages.alt: Mama kneeling to give Dzigbodi a warm, reassuring hug in the doorway, well clear of the broken blue cup pieces inside.

pages.text: After Mama safely cleared the shards, Dzigbodi swept the floor clean and placed her ball outside in the yard where it belonged. At once, her tummy stopped hurting. “Telling the truth felt hard,” she told Mama, “yet it feels much better than hiding.” Mama smiled. “I agree.”
sentences: After Mama safely cleared the shards, Dzigbodi swept the floor clean and placed her ball outside in the yard where it belonged.
At once, her tummy stopped hurting.
“Telling the truth felt hard,” she told Mama, “yet it feels much better than hiding.” Mama smiled.
“I agree.”
pages.alt: By the sunlit veranda steps, relieved Dzigbodi sets her small football outside in the courtyard while Mama smiles warmly holding a dustpan and broom.

activities.question: How did Dzigbodi feel while she was hiding what had happened?
What wise words did Mama share about trust?
options: A cup can be bought again, whereas trust cannot

items: The blue cup falls and breaks.
Dzigbodi shuts the door and feels worried.
She tells Mama the whole truth.
Mama clears the sharp pieces and they tidy up together.

activities.prompt: How does your heart feel after you tell the truth and help put a mistake right?

glossary.definition: Shattered or came apart into pieces after falling.
What really happened, told honestly without hiding.
Confidence that someone is honest and reliable.
